data.body_html:
Marbella’s coastline is one of the best places in the Mediterranean for dolphin watching, with common bottlenose and striped dolphins spotted year-round. But the time of day you choose for your yacht charter can change everything—from sea conditions and wildlife activity to the overall vibe. This guide compares morning and afternoon departures from Puerto Banús, so you can pick the slot that fits your group.

Why timing matters for dolphin watching

Dolphins are most active during feeding times, which often coincide with calmer seas. In Marbella, the sea breeze typically picks up around midday, making mornings (9am–1pm) generally flatter and more favourable for spotting dorsal fins. Afternoon charters (2pm–8pm) can still be excellent, especially if you prioritise sunset views and warmer swimming conditions.

Morning charters: calm seas, active dolphins

Morning trips from Puerto Banús head east towards Cabopino or west towards Estepona. The water is glassy, and dolphins often surface closer to shore. A 2-hour charter on the Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) is ideal for a quick sightseeing run. You’ll have the best light for photography, and the cooler air (around 24°C in summer) keeps everyone fresh. Morning charters also leave your afternoon free for other plans.

Afternoon charters: sunset, warmth, and relaxation

Afternoon departures let you combine dolphin watching with a swim stop at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where the water has warmed to 25–26°C. The light turns golden by 6pm, making for spectacular dolphin silhouettes. The Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h) is a favourite for groups wanting speed, space, and a free jet ski. Afternoon trips often feel more leisurely, with drinks flowing as the sun dips behind La Concha.

Sea conditions and dolphin behaviour

Morning seas in Marbella are typically Beaufort scale 1–2 (calm to light ripples). By 2pm, the thermal wind often pushes conditions to Beaufort 3–4 (small waves, occasional whitecaps). Dolphins prefer calmer water for hunting, so morning trips statistically yield more sightings. That said, afternoons are far from useless—dolphins still appear, and the trade-off is a more relaxed pace with a swim stop.

Best spots for dolphin watching near Marbella

  • Cala del Faro – 20 minutes from Puerto Banús; common bottlenose dolphin territory.
  • Cabo Pino – Shallow waters attract feeding pods.
  • Estepona – Westward route; often sees striped dolphins.
  • Río Verde – Close to Banús; good for short 2-hour trips.

Pricing comparison: morning vs afternoon

There’s no price difference between morning and afternoon for our fixed-rate boats. The Astondoa 40 costs €749 for 2 hours regardless of the slot. The Mangusta 80 is €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours. For other yachts like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is on request via WhatsApp. The real difference is value: morning trips pack more wildlife action into a shorter time; afternoon trips give you sunset and swimming.
